content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by us), preferred target.**

- **Responsive locations reviewed:** § 23.1–23.2 default/capacity reclamation (p0255–p0256), § 7.8–7.12 financial and extended payment charges (p0153–p0157), § 18 termination economics including the no-capital-cost-credit rule (p0228–p0235, p0233), and § 32 claims provisions. No clause uses "liquidated damages"; the penal effect sits in the reclamation mechanic.
- **Why it fails fallback:** on a persisting payment default our whole APCN 2 capacity may be reclaimed with *no payment or credit*, and we forfeit *all amounts already paid*, while accrued unpaid accounts remain due — a forfeiture unrelated to the size of the arrears that can exceed remaining contract value (walk-away territory).
- **Cure (two surgical replaces in 23.2, validated ok:true):** reclamation becomes compensated ("shall be entitled to payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity") and the forfeiture of amounts paid is replaced by an express statement that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable in respect of the default. Retained language on unpaid accounts stays intact and consistent.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the 300% extended payment charge (default interest on sums actually owed) and the no-capital-cost-credit rule on voluntary exit after the 25-year Initial Period.
